questions.question: A person watching a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person watching a placarded vehicle must be awake in the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded vehicle carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases) materials. Do not smoke or carry any lit cigarette, cigar, or pipe near vehicles with flammable or explosive materials.

questions.question: The engine of a placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's engine must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you need:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: Shipping papers must include:

options.text: How the materials will be used.

questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved:

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If the vehicle will travel fewer than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: You can only drive an improperly placarded vehicle when necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: While driving, shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or where you can reach them easily with your seat belt on. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always watch the nozzle and control the fuel flow while refueling.

questions.question: Which sign shows cargo may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Packaging can indicate if materials are hazardous. Cylinders and drums are commonly used to hold and transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, you should NOT use:
questions.explanation: Protect containers of hazardous materials from damage. Do not use hooks or equipment that could damage the containers.

questions.question: To choose the right placard, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: You must know the hazard class of the materials being shipped to choose the correct placard.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, you must:
questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan when transporting certain explosives. Avoid populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys.

questions.question: Hazardous materials warning signs on vehicles are usually what shape?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on all four sides.

questions.question: To complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest, you must:

options.text: Only sign it if you cross into another state.

questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. The manifest must be signed by hand.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must carry an approved gas mask in the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials cargo tanks, you must:

options.text: Slow down at railroad crossings, but you do not have to stop.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle has cargo tanks used for hazardous materials, you must stop at railroad crossings. This applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: If hazardous materials are leaking and you have no phone, you should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, do not move your vehicle more than necessary. Park your vehicle safely, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you have no phone, send someone else for help.

questions.question: A placard should be placed:

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder if space is limited.
On a background the same color as the placard.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: Placards must be at least three inches away from other markings. Keep them clear of doors, ladders, and attachments. Always place placards on a contrasting background color.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: Load corrosive containers one at a time by hand. Keep them upright. Do not drop or roll them.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training and testing?
questions.explanation: All drivers must be trained in hazardous materials safety. This includes recognizing and responding to security threats. Hazardous materials employees must receive training and testing at least once every three years.

questions.question: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, what must you do?

options.text: Write the hazardous materials in larger text.
Write the hazardous materials in red ink.

questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials must be listed first.

questions.question: What does the marine pollutant symbol look like?

options.text: A bird in a red octagon
A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol shows a fish in a white triangle with an X through it.

questions.question: If a "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, what else must the paper include?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means Column 2 contains a generic name. A generic name must be accompanied by the technical name.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, what should you do with the engine?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need the engine running to operate a pump.

questions.question: What must a driver have to accept a hazardous materials package (unless it appears unsafe)?
questions.explanation: Shippers certify that hazardous materials packages follow all regulations. You may accept the shipper's certification if the package does not appear unsafe or improperly packaged.

questions.question: What should a driver verify about shipping papers and packages?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping paper to the package markings and labels. Make sure the description and labels match correctly.

questions.question: How must a hazardous waste manifest be signed?

options.text: On the outside of the trailer.

questions.explanation: You must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest when transporting hazardous waste. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Which type of material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials require a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.
